scenes.tts: Are a young neuron's neurites truly equal? Or is one of them fixed as the axon from the start?
scenes.visual: Title card: Five Stages and a Race. Five identical neurites around a cell body; one question mark over each.
scenes.narration: Are a young neuron's neurites truly equal? Or is one of them fixed as the axon from the start?

scenes.tts: Gary Banker's laboratory grew neurons from the embryonic rat hippocampus. Most are pyramidal cells of one broad type.
scenes.visual: A small schematic of an embryonic rat brain with the hippocampus highlighted; an arrow leads to a dish of similar pyramidal outlines. Label: a fairly uniform population.
scenes.narration: Gary Banker's laboratory grew neurons from the embryonic rat hippocampus. Most are pyramidal cells of one broad type.

scenes.tts: Grown at low density, each neuron can be watched on its own.
scenes.visual: Zoom onto one neuron; a day counter appears in the corner.
scenes.narration: Grown at low density, each neuron can be watched on its own.

scenes.tts: In 1988, Carlos Dotti, C A Sullivan and Banker described five stages.
scenes.caption: In 1988, Carlos Dotti, C. A. Sullivan and Banker described five stages.
scenes.visual: On screen: Dotti, Sullivan and Banker, 1988. Five empty stage boxes.
scenes.narration: In 1988, Carlos Dotti, C. A. Sullivan and Banker described five stages.

scenes.tts: Stage one. Within hours of plating, the round cell spreads thin, flat veils of membrane.
scenes.visual: Stage 1 box fills: a round cell spreads lamellipodia. Label: lamellipodia. Day counter: hours.
scenes.narration: Stage one. Within hours of plating, the round cell spreads thin, flat veils of membrane.

scenes.tts: Stage two. The veils condense into several short neurites, all alike.
scenes.visual: Stage 2: five short neurites, equal length. On the right, a length-against-time plot starts with five overlapping traces.
scenes.narration: Stage two. The veils condense into several short neurites, all alike.

scenes.tts: Stage three. After a day or two, one neurite grows much faster than the rest. It becomes the axon.
scenes.visual: Stage 3: one neurite turns gold and lengthens; on the plot, one trace breaks away upward. Day counter: 1 to 2.
scenes.narration: Stage three. After a day or two, one neurite grows much faster than the rest. It becomes the axon.

scenes.tts: Stage four. Over the next few days, the other neurites grow, taper and branch as dendrites.
scenes.visual: Stage 4: the other neurites turn green, taper and branch.
scenes.narration: Stage four. Over the next few days, the other neurites grow, taper and branch as dendrites.

scenes.tts: Stage five. In the second week and later, spines form, and synapses multiply and mature.
scenes.visual: Stage 5: spines bud on the green dendrites; small synapse dots multiply. Day counter: week 2.
scenes.narration: Stage five. In the second week and later, spines form, and synapses multiply and mature.

scenes.tts: Back to stage two. The neurites look alike. That could mean two things.
scenes.visual: Rewind to stage 2: five equal neurites and five overlapping traces.
scenes.narration: Back to stage two. The neurites look alike. That could mean two things.

scenes.tts: Perhaps one was fixed for good as the axon.
scenes.visual: One neurite gets a tag labelled: fixed for good.
scenes.narration: Perhaps one was fixed for good as the axon.

scenes.tts: Or perhaps the choice is open, and they are competing.
scenes.visual: The tag stays in place; the five neurites are shown as runners at a start line. Label: can be reassigned.
scenes.narration: Or perhaps the choice is open, and they are competing.

scenes.tts: A young neuron's cut tests whether the choice can be undone.
scenes.visual: Card: the young neuron's cut. Can the choice be undone?
scenes.narration: A young neuron's cut tests whether the choice can be undone.

scenes.tts: Take a neuron just at stage three. Cut its leader back to the length of its siblings, erasing its lead.
scenes.visual: A blade shortens the gold neurite to the same length as the others; the gold trace drops to the pack.
scenes.narration: Take a neuron just at stage three. Cut its leader back to the length of its siblings, erasing its lead.

scenes.tts: If the axon was fixed for good, which process should grow out as the axon? And if the neurites compete?
scenes.visual: Two hypotheses on screen: fixed for good, or can be reassigned. Question mark over the neuron.
scenes.narration: If the axon was fixed for good, which process should grow out as the axon? And if the neurites compete?

scenes.tts: If the choice were fixed, the stump should regrow as the axon, whatever its length. Often, it did not.
scenes.visual: The cut removes the tagged neurite's lead and another neurite takes over, overriding the tag. The fixed-for-good card is struck through.
scenes.narration: If the choice were fixed, the stump should regrow as the axon, whatever its length. Often, it did not.

scenes.tts: In 1987, Carlos Dotti and Gary Banker found that another neurite, a future dendrite, could grow out as the axon.
scenes.visual: A green neurite turns gold and its trace takes off on the plot. On screen: Dotti and Banker, 1987.
scenes.narration: In 1987, Carlos Dotti and Gary Banker found that another neurite, a future dendrite, could grow out as the axon.

scenes.tts: Then Kimberly Goslin and Banker cut axons to different lengths.
scenes.visual: On screen: Goslin and Banker. Several neurons, each with its gold neurite cut to a different length.
scenes.narration: Then Kimberly Goslin and Banker cut axons to different lengths.

scenes.tts: When one remaining process was more than about ten micrometres longer than all the others, it became the axon.
scenes.caption: When one remaining process was more than about 10 micrometres longer than all the others, it became the axon.
scenes.visual: A ruler shows one process ahead of the rest by more than 10 micrometres; its trace resumes the climb. In some neurons it is the stump, in others a sibling.
scenes.narration: When one remaining process was more than about 10 micrometres longer than all the others, it became the axon.

scenes.tts: When the remaining processes were nearly equal, the new axon could not be predicted. It could be any of them, the cut one included.
scenes.visual: A cut level with the pack; in repeated runs a different trace breaks away each time, sometimes the cut one.
scenes.narration: When the remaining processes were nearly equal, the new axon could not be predicted. It could be any of them, the cut one included.

scenes.tts: So the choice can be undone. It behaves like a race, and length is part of the score.
scenes.visual: Runners on a track; a scoreboard reads: length.
scenes.narration: So the choice can be undone. It behaves like a race, and length is part of the score.

scenes.tts: Goslin and Banker proposed that uncut neurons choose the same way.
scenes.visual: An uncut neuron; its leading trace breaks away on the plot.
scenes.narration: Goslin and Banker proposed that uncut neurons choose the same way.

scenes.tts: The ten micrometre figure belongs to these experiments in cultured neurons. It is not a rule for every neuron.
scenes.caption: The 10 micrometre figure belongs to these experiments in cultured neurons. It is not a rule for every neuron.
scenes.visual: The number 10 micrometres shown inside a dish outline, with a small note: these cultures.
scenes.narration: The 10 micrometre figure belongs to these experiments in cultured neurons. It is not a rule for every neuron.

scenes.tts: The logic does not depend on the number. Get far enough ahead, and you win.
scenes.visual: The number fades; the arrow of the breaking-away trace remains.
scenes.narration: The logic does not depend on the number. Get far enough ahead, and you win.

scenes.tts: Stage two is a race. Next question: what kind of race has only one winner?
scenes.visual: Closing card: stage 2 is a race. Next: What Makes a Winner.
scenes.narration: Stage two is a race. Next question: what kind of race has only one winner?
